mainTopic: Lashes for kindling on יום טוב and the rule of מתוך; then whether חלה, the priestly gifts and תרומה may be brought to a כהן on יום טוב, and whether one may husk kernels on יום טוב.
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא that gives lashes for kindling a fire on יום טוב. רבי יוחנן rejects it. If the ברייתא is reliable, it can only follow בית שמאי, who do not accept the rule of מתוך: once something is allowed on יום טוב for a need, it is allowed even without one. A new משנה follows. בית שמאי forbid bringing חלה and the priestly gifts to a כהן on יום טוב, and בית הלל permit it. The two sides argue over whether these gifts are like תרומה, which may not be separated on יום טוב. The גמרא quotes three versions of this argument, from רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי and אחרים, and works out which ones fit the משנה. רבא shows that the משנה can fit רבי יהודה, and the גמרא adds that it can fit אחרים too. The only difference between those two is טפלה. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so even תרומה may be brought to a כהן on יום טוב, as the story of רב טובי's wine shows. Finally, רבא allows husking kernels on יום טוב. אביי challenges this twice, and the גמרא's answer to the second challenge, about separating תרומה, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The last item in the ברייתא: lashes for kindling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא recited before רבי יוחנן ends by listing lashes for הבערה, kindling a fire on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and he also gets lashes because of kindling a fire.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא that listed five sets of lashes for someone who cooks a גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב and eats it. This last item says he also gets lashes for kindling the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats kindling on יום טוב as a full לאו that earns lashes, just like on שבת. That claim is exactly what רבי יוחנן is about to attack in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Kindling a fire, one of the 39 מלאכות
He receives lashes (מלקות) for breaking a לאו
The sciatic nerve, which is forbidden to eat

phrases.english: because of kindling.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם הַבְעָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this ברייתא, kindling a fire on יום טוב, even for cooking, earns lashes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן throws the ברייתא out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the תנא to take this ברייתא outside, because lashes for kindling and cooking on יום טוב are not a reliable teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: Go out and teach that outside. Kindling and cooking are not a real משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects the ברייתא's claim that one gets lashes for kindling and cooking on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling the תנא to teach it outside means it does not belong in the study hall at all. The ברייתא gave lashes for both cooking on יום טוב and kindling, and רבי יוחנן says neither of these is a real source.

keyTerms.meaning: Go out and teach it outside, meaning this teaching is unreliable
Cooking
It is not a real teaching that we rely on

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying kindling is allowed for no reason on יום טוב. He is only saying it does not earn lashes, as the next steps explain.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go out and teach it outside,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן, speaking to the תנא who recited the ברייתא.

phrases.english: kindling and cooking are not a real teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹק תְּנִי לְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The parts of the ברייתא that give lashes for cooking and kindling on יום טוב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Since these actions are allowed on יום טוב for a need, they cannot carry lashes.

steps.title: If the ברייתא is reliable, it follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: If we must accept the ברייתא, it follows בית שמאי. They do not say that an action allowed on יום טוב for a need is also allowed without a need.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you insist it is a real teaching, it is בית שמאי. They say: we do not reason that since carrying out was allowed for a need, it was also allowed without a need. Here too, we do not reason that since kindling was allowed for a need, it was also allowed without a need.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a fallback. If the ברייתא is genuine, it fits only the view of בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on this daf, בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about carrying things out on יום טוב when there is no food need. בית שמאי do not accept the rule of מתוך, so kindling that serves no need stays a full מלאכה that earns lashes. By their view, the ברייתא makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you insist on saying
Since it was permitted. This is the start of the famous rule of מתוך
Carrying out from one domain to another
For a need, meaning for food on יום טוב

phrases.english: And if you insist on saying it is a real teaching —
it is בית שמאי, who say:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּתְּרָה הוֹצָאָה לְצוֹרֶךְ
phrases.english: we do not say: since carrying out was permitted for a need,
it was also permitted not for a need.
Here too, we do not say:
since kindling was permitted for a need,
it was also permitted not for a need.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצָא לוֹמַר מִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way to keep the ברייתא after rejecting it, by assigning it to בית שמאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution to a minority opinion that is not the הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might be a general teaching that everyone accepts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only בית שמאי, who reject מתוך, could hold that kindling earns lashes.

steps.title: Why it cannot follow בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל accept מתוך for carrying out, so they would also accept it for kindling. Kindling therefore does not earn lashes by their view.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if it were בית הלל: since they say that because carrying out was allowed for a need it was also allowed without a need, here too, because kindling was allowed for a need, it was also allowed without a need.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא cannot follow בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל hold that once a מלאכה is permitted on יום טוב for food, it is no longer a forbidden-with-lashes מלאכה on יום טוב even without food need. The same rule applies to kindling, so by בית הלל there are no lashes for it. Since the הלכה follows בית הלל, the ברייתא is not followed.

keyTerms.meaning: For if
Since they say

steps.whatToRemember: Under בית הלל's rule of מתוך, a מלאכה allowed on יום טוב for food (like kindling or carrying) does not earn lashes even when done without need. That is why רבי יוחנן rejects the ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of מתוך שהותרה לצורך הותרה נמי שלא לצורך, which the הלכה follows by בית הלל, shapes many laws of יום טוב.

phrases.english: For if it were בית הלל —

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמְרִי מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּתְּרָה הוֹצָאָה לְצוֹרֶךְ
phrases.english: since they say: since carrying out was permitted for a need
it was also permitted not for a need,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁהוּתְּרָה הַבְעָרָה לְצוֹרֶךְ —
phrases.english: here too: since kindling was permitted for a need —
it was also permitted not for a need.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the argument of step 3 by excluding בית הלל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: By בית הלל, kindling on יום טוב does not earn lashes, so the ברייתא can only follow בית שמאי.

steps.title: New משנה: bringing חלה and gifts to a כהן on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי forbid bringing חלה and the priestly gifts to a כהן on יום טוב, whether they were separated before יום טוב or on it. בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: one may not bring חלה and the gifts to the כהן on יום טוב, whether they were separated yesterday or today. And בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings another argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל about carrying on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing the gifts to the כהן involves carrying, but not for one's own food. This connects to the same disagreement about מתוך: בית שמאי forbid it, and בית הלל allow it. בית שמאי forbid it even if the gifts were separated today, on יום טוב itself.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, a new section of the משנה begins
The portion of dough given to a כהן
The priestly gifts from an animal: the foreleg, jaw, and maw
That were separated (set aside)
From yesterday, before יום טוב

phrases.english: משנה:
בית שמאי say: one may not bring
חלה and the gifts to the כהן on יום טוב,
whether they were separated yesterday,
or whether they were separated today.
And בית הלל permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מוֹלִיכִין חַלָּה וּמַתָּנוֹת לַכֹּהֵן בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic, still about carrying on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid bringing חלה and priestly gifts to a כהן on יום טוב. בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: בית שמאי compare the gifts to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי argue that חלה and the gifts are like תרומה. Since תרומה may not be brought to a כהן on יום טוב, the gifts may not be brought either.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: here is a comparison. חלה and the gifts are a gift to the כהן, and תרומה is a gift to the כהן. Just as we do not bring תרומה, so we do not bring the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי give a reason for their view from Step 5. Everyone agrees that תרומה may not be brought to a כהן on יום טוב, so the other gifts should follow the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a simple comparison. All of these items are gifts to a כהן. Since they belong to the same group, they should have the same יום טוב rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a comparison between two similar things
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Gifts to the כהן, here the portions from a slaughtered animal
One brings or carries (them to the כהן)

steps.confusionAlert: Here גזרה שוה does not mean the famous method of linking two פסוקים by a shared word. It just means 'these two are equal, so they share a rule.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה:
phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them: an analogy:
phrases.notes: Here this just means a comparison of two alike things, not the usual word-link between פסוקים.

phrases.english: Challah and the gifts are a gift to the priest,
and terumah is a gift to the priest.
Just as one may not bring terumah,
so too one may not bring the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית שמאי's reason for the ruling in Step 5
steps.raayaObject: בית שמאי's ruling that the gifts may not be brought on יום טוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The agreed rule that תרומה may not be brought on יום טוב

steps.title: בית הלל reject the comparison
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל point out a difference. תרומה may not be separated on יום טוב, but the gifts may be, so they may also be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: No. You may say this about תרומה, which one is not allowed to separate on יום טוב. But how can you say it about the gifts, which one is allowed to separate?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל break the comparison. They show that תרומה and the other gifts are different in one important way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on bringing תרומה comes from the fact that it may not even be separated on יום טוב. The gifts may be separated on יום טוב, so that reason does not apply to them. That is why they may be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted, allowed
Separating (the gift from the rest)
'If you said this about X, will you say it about Y?' A formula for showing that two cases are different

steps.whatToRemember: The two sides disagree over whether the gifts are like תרומה. בית הלל say they are different because the gifts may be separated on יום טוב and תרומה may not.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them: No,
if you said this about terumah,
where one is not allowed to separate it,
phrases.notes: He means separating it on יום טוב itself.

phrases.english: will you say it about the gifts,
where one is allowed to separate them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole comparison between תרומה and the other gifts
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תרומה may not be separated on יום טוב, but the gifts may be, so the two are not alike

steps.title: Whose view does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא first assumes that 'separated today' means the animal was slaughtered today. It then asks whose opinion the משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: You might think 'separated today' means slaughtered today, and 'separated last night' means slaughtered last night. If so, whose view is our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts by reading the משנה in a simple way. Then it asks which תנא holds this view. This step sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the gifts are separated on the same day the animal is slaughtered. This means בית שמאי forbid even gifts from an animal slaughtered on יום טוב itself. That is a strict view, so the גמרא wants to know who holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think (an assumption the גמרא checks)
Were separated
Were slaughtered
Whose view is our משנה?

phrases.english: GEMARA: It enters your mind
that 'separated today' means slaughtered today,
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words from Step 5, about gifts separated before יום טוב or on it.

phrases.english: and 'separated last evening' means slaughtered last evening.
Whose view is the mishnah?

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ שֶׁהוּרְמוּ מֵהַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה from Step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds the משנה's view, if 'separated' means 'slaughtered' on that day

steps.title: It follows אחרים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows neither רבי יוסי nor רבי יהודה. It follows the sage called אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not רבי יוסי and not רבי יהודה, but אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question and names the opinion behind the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two well-known views are ruled out, so the משנה must follow a third opinion, אחרים. The next step brings a source to show why רבי יהודה does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Others', a name used for an unnamed תנא

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Not Rabbi Yosei and not Rabbi Yehuda,
but Acherim.
phrases.notes: Literally 'others'. This is a name for a תנא whose name is not given.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, אֶלָּא אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows אחרים, not רבי יוסי or רבי יהודה

steps.title: רבי יהודה's version of the argument
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה limits the argument. He says all agree that gifts from before יום טוב may be brought together with today's gifts. They argue only about bringing them by themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא, רבי יהודה said: בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that gifts separated before יום טוב may be brought along with gifts separated and slaughtered today. They argue only about bringing them alone. בית שמאי say we do not bring them, and בית הלל say we do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה to show that his view does not match the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says yesterday's gifts may be brought along with gifts separated and slaughtered today. That assumes everyone allows today's gifts. But under the reading of step 8, the משנה has בית שמאי forbidding even gifts from an animal slaughtered today. So the משנה cannot be רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
They did not disagree
By themselves, alone
The day before יום טוב

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַמַּתָּנוֹת שֶׁהוּרְמוּ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
phrases.english: about gifts separated on the eve of the Festival
that one may bring them along with the gifts
separated today and slaughtered today.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא לְהוֹלִיכָן בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָן,
phrases.english: They disagreed only about bringing them by themselves,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the gifts separated before יום טוב.

phrases.english: for Beit Shammai say: one may not bring them,
and Beit Hillel say: one may bring them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 9 by showing that רבי יהודה's view differs from the משנה
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה is not רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה, where בית שמאי allow yesterday's gifts together with today's

steps.title: בית שמאי's comparison in רבי יהודה's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Within רבי יהודה's ברייתא, בית שמאי make the same comparison to תרומה found in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is how בית שמאי reasoned: חלה and the gifts are a gift to the כהן, and תרומה is a gift to the כהן. Just as we do not bring תרומה, so we do not bring the gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and gives בית שמאי's reason in רבי יהודה's version of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as in the משנה. The difference is what they apply to. In רבי יהודה's version, the comparison only forbids bringing gifts by themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Reasoned, argued

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a mistake or a repeat of the משנה. These words are part of רבי יהודה's ברייתא, which uses the same argument for a narrower case.

phrases.english: And this is how Beit Shammai would reason:
Challah and the gifts are a gift to the priest,
and terumah is a gift to the priest.
Just as one may not bring terumah,
so too one may not bring the gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָךְ הָיוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי דָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהודה's ברייתא with בית שמאי's reasoning
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי יהודה's version, בית שמאי compare the gifts to תרומה to forbid bringing them alone

steps.title: בית הלל's answer in רבי יהודה's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: In the ברייתא, בית הלל give the same answer. Unlike תרומה, the gifts may be separated on יום טוב, so they may be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: No. You may say this about תרומה, which one is not allowed to separate. But how can you say it about the gifts, which one is allowed to separate?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with בית הלל rejecting the comparison, just as they did in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's reasoning is unchanged: the gifts may be separated on יום טוב, and תרומה may not. So in רבי יהודה's version, בית הלל allow even gifts from before יום טוב to be brought alone.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה teaches that the argument is only about bringing yesterday's gifts by themselves, since everyone allows yesterday's gifts together with today's. Both the משנה and his ברייתא use the same comparison to תרומה. Whether the משנה really excludes רבי יהודה is reopened in steps 17-22.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them: No,
if you said this about terumah,
where one is not allowed to separate it,
will you say it about the gifts,
where one is allowed to separate them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית שמאי's comparison within the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: בית שמאי's comparison to תרומה in רבי יהודה's version
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The gifts may be separated on יום טוב and תרומה may not, so they are not alike

steps.title: רבי יוסי: the argument was only about תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says בית שמאי and בית הלל agree that the gifts may be brought on יום טוב. They argue only about תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about the gifts. Everyone agrees they may be brought. They argued only about תרומה. בית שמאי say it may not be brought, and בית הלל say it may be brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives a second version of the argument, from רבי יוסי. In his version, the gifts are not in question at all; only תרומה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's version, the gifts were partly argued about and תרומה was forbidden by everyone. רבי יוסי moves the argument over to תרומה, and he says everyone permits the gifts. So even בית שמאי agree the gifts may be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not argue
One may bring (carry) it to the כהן
The portion of produce given to the כהן
The gifts from an animal (foreleg, cheeks, stomach) given to the כהן

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not argue
about the gifts, that one may bring them;
they argued only about the teruma,
for Beit Shammai say: one may not bring it,
and Beit Hillel say: one may bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, competing version of the dispute after רבי יהודה's version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone permits bringing the gifts. The argument is only about תרומה: בית שמאי forbid it and בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: בית הלל's reasoning: all gifts to the כהן are alike
steps.stepSummary: In רבי יוסי's version, בית הלל compare תרומה to חלה and the gifts. Since the gifts may be brought, so may תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is how בית הלל reasoned: חלה and the gifts are a gift to the כהן, and תרומה is a gift to the כהן. Just as one may bring the gifts, so too one may bring תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל explain why they permit bringing תרומה. This sets up בית שמאי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is a simple comparison. All of these are presents for the כהן, and everyone agrees the gifts may be brought. So בית הלל say תרומה should be treated the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: They reasoned, made a logical argument
The portion of dough given to the כהן
Just as ... so too

steps.confusionAlert: In רבי יהודה's version (steps 11-12), בית שמאי made this comparison and בית הלל answered it. In רבי יוסי's version the roles are switched: בית הלל make the comparison and בית שמאי answer.

phrases.english: And this is how Beit Hillel would reason:
Ḥalla and the gifts are a gift to the priest,
and teruma is a gift to the priest;
just as one may bring the gifts,
so too one may bring the teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָךְ הָיוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל דָּנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בית הלל's reason for their ruling in רבי יוסי's version.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומה is like the other gifts to the כהן, so it may be brought on יום טוב.

steps.title: בית שמאי reject the comparison
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer that the gifts may be separated on יום טוב, but תרומה may not. So the two cannot be compared.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: No! You said this about the gifts, which one is allowed to separate on יום טוב. Will you say the same about תרומה, which one is not allowed to separate on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי knock down בית הלל's comparison by pointing to a real difference between the gifts and תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gifts may be separated on יום טוב, so bringing them fits the day. תרומה may not be separated on יום טוב, so בית שמאי say it may not be brought either. This is the same answer from steps 11-12, but now it is given by the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted, allowed
Separating (setting aside) the gift
No! If you said ... (a formula for rejecting a comparison)

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them: No!
If you said this about the gifts,
which one is permitted to separate,
phrases.notes: He means separating them on יום טוב itself.

phrases.english: will you say it about teruma,
which one is not permitted to separate?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית שַׁמַּאי: לֹא, אִם אֲמַרְתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית הלל's comparison in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the gifts and תרומה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The gifts may be separated on יום טוב, but תרומה may not, so they are not alike.

steps.title: אחרים: the argument was only about the gifts
steps.stepSummary: אחרים say everyone agrees תרומה may not be brought. The argument is only about the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: אחרים say: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about תרומה. Everyone agrees it may not be brought. They argued only about the gifts. בית שמאי say they may not be brought, and בית הלל say they may be brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third version of the argument, from the sage called אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, תרומה is forbidden by everyone, and the argument is only about the gifts. Unlike רבי יהודה, אחרים do not say that some cases of gifts are agreed on by everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'others'; the name used for a particular תנא

phrases.english: Aḥerim say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not argue
about teruma, that one may not bring it;
they argued only about the gifts,
for Beit Shammai say: one may not bring them,
and Beit Hillel say: one may bring them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל עַל הַתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third version of the dispute, after רבי יהודה's and רבי יוסי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone forbids bringing תרומה. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about the gifts.

steps.title: Suggestion: the משנה follows אחרים, not רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: With all three versions laid out, the גמרא suggests that the משנה matches only אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה follows אחרים and not רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states its suggestion outright: the משנה matches אחרים and does not fit רבי יהודה. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This depends on the assumption from step 8 that 'separated today' means 'slaughtered today.' רבי יהודה said everyone permits gifts from an animal slaughtered today, but the משנה has a dispute. So it seems the משנה cannot follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion)

phrases.english: Shall we say it is Aḥerim
and not Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא אֲחֵרִים הִיא וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the three versions just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the משנה limited to אחרים's view, so it cannot follow רבי יהודה?

steps.title: רבא: 'separated today' does not mean 'slaughtered today'
steps.stepSummary: רבא points out that the משנה only says the gifts were separated today. The animal could have been slaughtered yesterday, which is exactly רבי יהודה's case of the dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Does the משנה say 'separated today and slaughtered today'? It only says 'separated.' Really, the animal was slaughtered yesterday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the assumption from step 8. He shows the משנה can fit רבי יהודה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the dispute is about gifts from an animal slaughtered before יום טוב. If the animal was slaughtered yesterday and the gifts were only separated today, the משנה is describing exactly that case. So nothing forces the משנה away from רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach...? (questions what the text actually says)
That were separated
From yesterday (before יום טוב)
And really, actually

phrases.english: Rava said:
Does it teach: 'that were separated today
and that were slaughtered today'?
It teaches only 'that were separated,'
and really, they were slaughtered yesterday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִי קָתָנֵי שֶׁהוּרְמוּ מֵהַיּוֹם וְשֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ מֵהַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion in step 17 by undoing the assumption from step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the משנה cannot follow רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumed 'separated today' means 'slaughtered today.'

steps.title: Then the משנה follows רבי יהודה, not אחרים?
steps.stepSummary: Now that the משנה fits רבי יהודה, the גמרא asks whether it can still fit אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then shall we say the משנה follows רבי יהודה and not אחרים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the question. Now it suggests that the משנה matches רבי יהודה and does not fit אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבא's reading, the משנה is about animals slaughtered yesterday, which matches רבי יהודה's case. The question is whether אחרים, who did not mention this detail, can also fit.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is Rabbi Yehuda
and not Aḥerim?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא וְלֹא אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבא's reading. Now the משנה seems to fit only רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רבא's reading rule out אחרים?

steps.title: It can also follow אחרים, about animals slaughtered yesterday
steps.stepSummary: Even אחרים can be understood as talking about animals slaughtered before יום טוב, so the משנה fits them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows אחרים. They are also talking about animals that were slaughtered yesterday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה does not have to exclude אחרים. Their dispute can also be about animals slaughtered yesterday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים never said which animals they meant. So the גמרא reads their dispute as being about the same case as רבי יהודה's: animals slaughtered before יום טוב. With that reading, the משנה fits both views.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say...
About those (cases)

phrases.english: You can even say it is Aḥerim,
and they argued about those that were slaughtered yesterday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by reading אחרים as also talking about animals slaughtered yesterday.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחרים's dispute can also be about animals slaughtered before יום טוב, so the משנה fits them as well.

steps.title: Then אחרים say the same thing as רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: If both are talking about animals slaughtered yesterday, it seems there is no difference between רבי יהודה and אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If אחרים also mean animals slaughtered yesterday, they seem to be saying exactly what רבי יהודה says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate opinions are recorded, so they should differ somehow. If both make the dispute about gifts from animals slaughtered before יום טוב, what is left to tell them apart?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
This is the same as

phrases.english: If so,
this is the same as Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי הַיְינוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of אחרים in step 20
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If אחרים and רבי יהודה describe the same dispute, there is no reason to record them as two different opinions.

steps.title: The difference: טפלה, old gifts brought along with today's
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה and אחרים differ about טפלה: gifts from before יום טוב brought together with gifts separated today.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: טפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is still a real difference between the two views. They disagree about טפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said all agree that older gifts may be brought along together with today's gifts. אחרים did not say this, so for them this case is also part of the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
Secondary: older gifts brought along together with today's gifts

steps.whatToRemember: There are three versions of the argument. רבי יוסי says it is about תרומה. רבי יהודה and אחרים say it is about the gifts, and the משנה can follow either one. The only difference between those two is טפלה, which רבי יהודה says everyone permits.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא saves a משנה for more than one view by carefully reading its words ('separated' and not 'slaughtered'). It then makes sure each opinion still says something different.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: secondary gifts.
phrases.notes: These are gifts separated before יום טוב that a person brings along together with gifts separated today.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ טְפֵלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21 by finding a practical difference between the two views.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a practical difference between two opinions that seemed identical
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה and אחרים seemed to say exactly the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ about טפלה. רבי יהודה says everyone permits it, while for אחרים it is part of the dispute.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, in the name of שמואל, rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: After the long discussion, the גמרא gives a final ruling: we follow רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יוסי's version, everyone (even בית שמאי) allows bringing the gifts, and בית הלל allow bringing even תרומה. Since we follow בית הלל, the practical result is that even תרומה may be brought to a כהן on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion
The תנא whose view about bringing gifts on יום טוב is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, one may bring gifts such as תרומה to a כהן on יום טוב, following רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion of the dispute with a practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical law follows רבי יוסי: the gifts, and even תרומה, may be brought to a כהן on יום טוב.

steps.title: רב טובי asks about bringing תרומה wine to a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רב טובי had a jug of תרומה wine. He asks רב יוסף whether he may bring it to a כהן on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טובי, son of רב נחמיה, had a jug of תרומה wine. He came to רב יוסף and asked: may I bring it to a כהן today, on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real question. It is setting up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the kind of case רבי יוסי's view is about: carrying a gift to a כהן on יום טוב. The story will show the ruling being used in real life.

keyTerms.meaning: A jug or barrel
The portion of produce given to a כהן
To bring or carry over

phrases.english: Rav Tovi, son of Rav Nechemya,
had a jug of teruma wine.
He came before Rav Yosef.
He said to him: What is the law about bringing it
to a kohen now?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ לְאַמְטוֹיֵי לְכֹהֵן הָאִידָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a real-life case where the ruling just given applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May one bring תרומה wine to a כהן on יום טוב?

steps.title: רב יוסף answers with שמואל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers by quoting שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי, so it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question by quoting the ruling we just learned. So רב טובי may bring the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not say "yes" directly. He quotes the ruling instead. In רבי יוסי's version, בית הלל allow bringing even תרומה on יום טוב, so the answer is that the תרומה wine may be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he said

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Yehuda said
that Shmuel said: The halacha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב טובי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted, because the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.

steps.title: A host asks about crushing mustard stalks on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The host of רבא בר רב חנן asks whether he may crush mustard stalks and eat the seeds on יום טוב. רבא בר רב חנן does not know, so he goes to ask רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The host of רבא בר רב חנן had bundles of mustard stalks. He asked: may I crush them and eat from them on יום טוב? רבא בר רב חנן did not know the answer, so he went to רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with a new story. The גמרא is setting up רבא's ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing stalks to get the seeds out looks like threshing, which is a kind of work. The question is whether this small amount of crushing for eating is allowed on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A host who gives someone lodging
Bundles of stalks
Mustard
To crush or rub the seeds out

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people here: רבא בר רב חנן, the guest who is asked, and רבא, the great אמורא he goes to ask.

phrases.english: The host of Rava bar Rav Chanan
had bundles of mustard stalks.
He said to him: What is the law about crushing them
and eating from them on Yom Tov?
He did not have it in hand,
phrases.notes: An expression meaning he did not know the answer.

phrases.english: so he came before Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ לְפָרוֹכֵי וּמֵיכַל מִנַּיְיהוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unconnected to the תרומה discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May one crush mustard stalks to eat the seeds on יום טוב?

steps.title: רבא: husking kernels and crushing legumes is allowed on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that one may husk kernels and crush legumes on יום טוב, so the mustard may be crushed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: One may rub kernels to husk them, and one may crush legumes, on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers with a general rule: small-scale husking and crushing for food is allowed on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mustard case is just like the cases in רבא's rule. If kernels and legumes may be rubbed out on יום טוב, mustard seeds may be too.

keyTerms.meaning: Rubbing kernels between the fingers to remove the husks
Crushing to get the seeds out
Legumes (beans and the like)

phrases.english: He said to him: One may rub kernels to husk them
and crush legumes on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹלְלִין מְלִילוֹת וּמְפָרְכִין קִטְנִיּוֹת בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the host's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Husking and crushing for food is permitted on יום טוב.

steps.title: אביי challenges from a ברייתא: the שבת case
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא. Kernels husked on ערב שבת may be blown clean by hand on שבת, but not with a basket or a large dish.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: If someone husked kernels on ערב שבת, the next day he may blow away the chaff by passing them from hand to hand and eat. But he may not use a basket or a large dish.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins an attack on רבא's ruling by quoting a ברייתא. This first part, about שבת, sets up the יום טוב part that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lets someone clean the kernels on שבת only in an unusual way, from hand to hand. Notice that the husking itself was done the day before, on ערב שבת. That detail will matter for אביי's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a תנאי source
Blows away the chaff (winnows)
A basket
A large dish

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
One who husks kernels on Shabbat eve,
on the next day may blow away the chaff from hand to hand, and eat.
But not with a basket, and not with a large dish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against רבא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that one may husk kernels on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes husking only on the day before, which hints that husking on the holy day itself is not allowed.

steps.title: The יום טוב case: husking is allowed only on the day before
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: kernels husked on ערב יום טוב may be cleaned on יום טוב a little at a time, even with a basket or dish, but not with real sifting tools. The גמרא reads the wording to mean husking is allowed on ערב יום טוב, but not on יום טוב itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone husked kernels on ערב יום טוב, the next day he may blow away the chaff a little at a time and eat, even with a basket or a large dish. But not with a tray, a winnowing sieve, or a sifter. So: on ערב יום טוב, yes; on יום טוב itself, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the יום טוב case, and then אביי draws his challenge from it. The ברייתא only allows husking that was done on ערב יום טוב, which goes against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יום טוב is more lenient than שבת, since a basket or dish may be used. Still, the ברייתא speaks only of kernels husked the day before. That suggests husking on יום טוב itself is forbidden, and רבא allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: A little at a time

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two actions. Cleaning off the chaff on יום טוב is allowed here. The question is about husking, the rubbing, done on יום טוב itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב — אִין, בְּיוֹם טוֹב — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's quote and states the inference that challenges רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that one may husk kernels and crush legumes on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows eating kernels only when they were husked on ערב יום טוב. This implies husking on יום טוב itself is forbidden, which contradicts רבא.

steps.title: The ברייתא's wording may just copy its first part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא may allow husking even on יום טוב. It only said 'from ערב יום טוב' to match its first part, which said 'from ערב שבת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the ברייתא allows husking on יום טוב itself. Since the first part said 'from ערב שבת', the last part also said 'from ערב יום טוב' to match.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the ברייתא's wording in step 29. It says the wording 'from ערב יום טוב' does not prove that husking is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, husking really is forbidden, so the first part had to say 'from ערב שבת'. The last part used the same phrase only so that the two halves would match. It does not mean husking on יום טוב itself is forbidden, so רבא's ruling still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say; a way of showing the other side is also possible
Since; because of (here: because the first part said it, the second part copied it)
The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying 'ערב יום טוב' means יום טוב. The words still say ערב. The point is that the wording only matches the first part, so you cannot draw a rule from it.

phrases.english: You can even say it means on יום טוב itself,

steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'From ערב יום טוב' seemed to mean husking is forbidden on יום טוב itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase only matches the first part's 'from ערב שבת'. Husking on יום טוב may still be allowed, so רבא is not disproved.

steps.title: If husking is allowed, a person would separate תרומה on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא. Allowing husking on יום טוב would mean separating תרומה on יום טוב, but the משנה says this is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we have found a case where a person may separate תרומה on יום טוב. But we learned in the משנה: 'No, if you said this about תרומה, which one may not separate on יום טוב, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new challenge against רבא. This time it comes from the laws of תרומה, not from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Husking finishes the grain as food. Once that happens, תרומה must be separated before eating. So if husking were allowed on יום טוב, one would have to separate תרומה on יום טוב. But the משנה clearly says תרומה may not be separated on יום טוב, so husking should be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce that must be given to a כֹּהֵן
Allowed; entitled
Separating (setting aside) the תרומה
And we learned in a משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a rule allowing one action (husking) can lead to a forbidden result (separating תרומה). The גמרא must explain how both can be true.

phrases.english: If so, we have found a case of תרומה
phrases.notes: He means: if husking is allowed on יום טוב, as רבא said.

phrases.english: that one is allowed to separate on יום טוב,
but we learned in a משנה:
"No, if you said this about תרומה,"
"which one is not allowed to separate, etc."!
phrases.notes: 'Etc.' means the משנה continues. The part that matters here is that תרומה may not be separated on יום טוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן מָצִינוּ תְּרוּמָה שֶׁזַּכַּאי בַּהֲרָמָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the wording challenge was answered, אביי attacks רבא from a new direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling in step 27 that one may husk kernels and crush legumes on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Husking makes the grain a finished food, so it now needs תרומה separated. Allowing husking on יום טוב would mean separating תרומה on יום טוב, which the משנה forbids.

steps.title: The גמרא begins to answer: there is no difficulty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens its answer to אביי's challenge by saying 'it is not difficult'. The explanation comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is announcing that it has an answer to אביי's challenge, and the actual answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא קשיא' tells us the גמרא will show how husking on יום טוב can be allowed without contradicting the משנה about תרומה. The details are not given here yet.
